[[File:SWTCG Attack of the Clones booster display.jpg|thumb|right|220px|''Attack of the Clones'' booster display, the first SWTCG set.<ref name="aotcbox">[http://www.wizards.com/global/images/swtcg_expansion_aotc_productShot_en.jpg ''Attack of the Clones'' product shot], wizards.com. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060625042505/http://www.wizards.com/global/images/swtcg_expansion_aotc_productShot_en.jpg Internet Archive]</ref>]]
'''''Star Wars'' Trading Card Game''' (SWTCG) is the collectible card game Wizards of the Coast published from April 2002 under the ''Star Wars'' trading-card license that Lucasfilm moved from Decipher. ''Magic: The Gathering'' creator Richard Garfield designed it.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Trading_Card_Game Star Wars Trading Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260202232757/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Trading_Card_Game Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="icv2-2002">[https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/983/wizards-coast-gets-star-wars-ccg Wizards of the Coast Gets Star Wars CCG], ICv2 (1 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008201620/https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/983/wizards-coast-gets-star-wars-ccg Internet Archive]</ref> It used all-new mechanics and was not compatible with [[Star Wars CCG]].<ref name="icv2-2002" /> Players fight for control of three arenas (Space, Ground and Character) and win by controlling two.<ref name="wp" />

== Organized play ==

Wizards ran SWTCG through DCI-sanctioned tournaments and championship events, with the second annual championship at Gen Con in July 2003 and $20,000 in prize support.<ref name="toymania">[http://www.toymania.com/toyshows/tf2003/full/hasbro_swtcg.shtml Star Wars Trading Card Game – Battle of Yavin], Toymania, Toy Fair 2003. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260206125220/https://www.toymania.com/toyshows/tf2003/full/hasbro_swtcg.shtml Internet Archive]</ref>

== End ==

On 31 October 2005 Wizards confirmed that SWTCG was on "indefinite hold", cancelling unreleased sets including ''Rise of the Empire''; a spokesperson said fans' attention had shifted to the Star Wars miniatures.<ref name="icv2-2005">[https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/7753/star-wars-tcg-indefinite-hold Star Wars TCG on 'Indefinite Hold'], ICv2 (31 October 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20060317085156/http://www.icv2.com/articles/news/7753.html Internet Archive]</ref> Wizards let its ''Star Wars'' license expire in 2010.<ref name="icv2-2010">[https://icv2.com/print/article/16762 WotC Drops Star Wars License], ICv2 (31 January 2010). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20100204020944/http://www.icv2.com/articles/news/16762.html Internet Archive]</ref> A fan Independent Development Committee has released free SWTCG sets since.<ref name="wp" /><ref name="idc">[https://swtcgidc.wordpress.com/ Star Wars Trading Card Game: Independent Development Committee]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010134005/https://swtcgidc.wordpress.com/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== SWCCG players and SWTCG ==

Decipher's [[Warren Holland]] called the new game "totally incompatible" with Decipher's and the move "disrespectful" to existing customers.<ref name="icv2-2002" /> A TheForce.Net preview described SWCCG fans' reactions as ranging from outrage to reluctant acceptance, with most taking a "wait and see" attitude.<ref name="tfnrev">[https://www.theforce.net/tcg/swtcg_review.asp Star Wars TCG Review], TheForce.Net (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20160413032454/http://www.theforce.net/tcg/swtcg_review.asp Internet Archive]</ref> Early SWCCG players on TheForce.Net boards called it a possible "side game" rather than a replacement.<ref name="tfnboard">[https://boards.theforce.net/threads/first-impression-of-sw-tcg.6383903/ First Impression of SW:TCG], TheForce.Net boards (2002). Preserved copy: none yet (Wayback save failed 13 October 2026)</ref> Meanwhile the [[Players Committee]] kept SWCCG going with Virtual cards; see [[History of Star Wars CCG]].

== Relationship to SWCCG ==

Before SWTCG was released, Wizards of the Coast flew several SWCCG players, among them [[Jonny Chu]] and [[Paul Todd Feldman]], out for a weekend of playtesting. Both later described the playtest in 2025 video interviews.<ref name="chu">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JLkMOP3rLQ8&t=1072s SWCCG PDS2: Jonny Chu Interview & HB X-wings], Bill Bisco, YouTube (28 April 2025), 17:52–18:19. Preserved copy: none yet (Wayback save failed 13 October 2026)</ref><ref name="torch">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I&t=207s SWCCG PDS2: DRTORCH Worlds Finalist 1996,1997,1999,2000 Interview, MWYHL 2Test], Bill Bisco, YouTube (29 May 2025), 3:27–4:10. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260929064953/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive]</ref>

Chu said the players met Richard Garfield and toured the Hasbro library. At the end of the weekend Wizards asked each player whether they would play the game, and the players answered no, one by one. He said the game was "all premised on dice", so a player could invest a lot of time and still lose to bad rolls. His verdict was that it was "total trash", though he said Wizards "rolled out the red carpet" for the testers.<ref name="chu2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JLkMOP3rLQ8&t=1117s SWCCG PDS2: Jonny Chu Interview & HB X-wings], Bill Bisco, YouTube (28 April 2025), 18:37–19:04. Preserved copy: none yet (Wayback save failed 13 October 2026)</ref>

Feldman said he gave Wizards "neutral feedback" and that they used it, but his own view was that the game "was horrible. It was nothing like this. This is strategy", comparing it with SWCCG.<ref name="torch" />
